headline: South Asia: Iraq PM hails new era of 'sovereignty' after US-led coalition exit
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Iraq PM hails new era of 'sovereignty' after US-led coalition exit.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy: main target of overnight strike was energy infrastructure in capital and Kyiv Oblast.
- Africa: Multiple reports claim Netanyahu was warned ahead of Hamas' 2023 attack.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon awards Raytheon up to $20.7 billion to nearly double AMRAAM production.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: Pentagon awards Raytheon up to $20.7 billion to nearly double AMRAAM production.
The Defense Department has awarded Raytheon a multiyear contract worth up to $20.7 billion to build Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missiles, or AMRAAMs.
- Military Times, 13 hours ago: US Navy taps 3 firms to build MUSVs for around $40M per vessel.
The U.S. Navy announced Tuesday that it is awarding contracts to three defense companies for the production of 30 medium unmanned surface vessels.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: Pentagon directs cyber, intelligence agencies to counter foreign election threats.
Hegseth ordered the agencies to "mobilize every authorized asset, capability and partnership under your command" to defend U.S. election infrastructure.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: USS Klakring sent to the bottom of the Atlantic in joint US-UK SINKEX.
A decommissioned U.S. guided-missile frigate was sent to the bottom of the Atlantic on Sept. 25 during a joint U.S.-U.K. naval exercise.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Zelenskyy: main target of overnight strike was energy infrastructure in capital and Kyiv Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Zelenskyy: main target of overnight strike was energy infrastructure in capital and Kyiv Oblast.
President Zelenskyy has reported that five people were killed and 14 injured when Russian drones and ballistic missiles hit energy facilities in Kyiv Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Ukrainian forces hit Russian drone depot, command post and logistics facilities.
Ukraine’s General Staff has confirmed strikes on a Russian UAV depot in Hranitne, a command post in Lysychansk and logistics facilities in Donetsk, Luhansk and Crimea.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Utility company worker killed in Russian drone attack on Kyiv.
A Kyivteploenergo employee has been killed in a Russian drone attack on Kyiv's Solomianskyi district on Wednesday morning. [Kyivteploenergo is the largest municipal heat and hot water supplier in Kyiv – ed.]
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: "It will be a dark winter for Europe": Belgium predicts increase in Russian hybrid attacks.
Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken has warned that Russian hybrid attacks on Europe will increase in the coming months and called for stronger air defence using Ukrainian technologies.
Southern Europe - bottom line: US Prosecutor Questions Kosovo’s Failure to Mitigate Thaci Verdict Expectations.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: US Prosecutor Questions Kosovo’s Failure to Mitigate Thaci Verdict Expectations.
Clint Williamson recalls investigating the four guerrilla commanders recently convicted of war crimes, questions Kosovo’s failure to temper public expectations of an acquittal, and ponders the future of international justice at a time of “dysfunctionality” in the UN Security Council.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Multiple reports claim Netanyahu was warned ahead of Hamas' 2023 attack.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: Multiple reports claim Netanyahu was warned ahead of Hamas' 2023 attack.
Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu has denied receiving advance knowledge of the 7 October 2023 offensive, claiming that security chiefs did not warn him.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Nigeria: Tinubu Urges UN Security Council to Sanction Nuclear Weapons Proliferation.
[Leadership] President Bola Tinubu has called on the United Nations Security Council to take stronger action against the spread of weapons of mass destruction and intensify efforts towards the complete elimination of nuclear weapons.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Congolese politician beaten to death after promoting Ebola awareness.
A Congolese politician has been beaten to death after promoting Ebola awareness during a radio interview. Marie-Celestin Karondwa from the ruling UDPS party was attacked on Sunday by residents of Butembo, in DR Congo's North Kivu province.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one day ago: Ethiopia: Escalating Northern Ethiopia Conflict Overwhelms Hospitals - MSF Reports.
[Reporter] Renewed fighting across northern Ethiopia has driven hundreds of war-wounded patients into hospitals across the Tigray and Amhara regions, straining medical facilities and forcing Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to suspend some operations and redirect staff.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Malawi Moves Towards Advanced Cancer Treatment With Nuclear Medicine Facilities.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Malawi: Malawi Moves Towards Advanced Cancer Treatment With Nuclear Medicine Facilities.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi is on the brink of a major breakthrough in the fight against cancer, with advanced diagnosis and treatment facilities known as nuclear medicine set to launch in Lilongwe, dramatically boosting access to life-saving cancer care for thousands of desperate patients.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: South Africa: Cases of Murdered Ekurhuleni Women Will Not Go Cold.
[SAnews.gov.za] President Cyril Ramaphosa has assured the families of the women who have been brutally killed and whose bodies were discovered in Ekurhuleni that their cases will not be allowed to go cold.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Nigeria: Xenophobia - Nigerian Consulate Condemns Killing of Three Nigerians in South Africa.
[Vanguard] The Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Nigeria in Johannesburg has condemned the deaths of three Nigerian nationals killed in different parts of South Africa in less than one week, between September 18 and 21, 2026.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Gauteng e-Panic Button Attempted Security Breach Thwarted.
[SAnews.gov.za] The Gauteng Department of e-Government has moved to reassure residents that the Gauteng e-Panic Button mobile application is safe to use after media reports raised concerns about information security risks.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israel’s Lapid accuses Netanyahu of ‘fear-mongering’ over attack warning.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Israel’s Lapid accuses Netanyahu of ‘fear-mongering’ over attack warning.
Opposition leader dismisses Netanyahu's warning of possible attacks during next month's general election.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Public workers in France strike over pay as student protests turn violent.
Tens of thousands of workers march nationwide, as police arrest 440 students in clashes at schools.
- Jerusalem Post, 23 hours ago: Hamas official's arrest in Gaza gave Israel intelligence surge to kill top terrorists - exclusive.
Three Hamas brigade commanders have been killed since September 11, following the September 2 capture of senior Hamas security official Mu'in al-Arabid in Gaza.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Iran is renewing progress on its nuclear program, Netanyahu tells UAE President MBZ - report.
According to the report, the information Netanyahu presented included details about new construction work at the mountainous site known as “Pickaxe Mountain,” about 140 miles south of Tehran.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Iraq PM hails new era of 'sovereignty' after US-led coalition exit.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Iraq PM hails new era of 'sovereignty' after US-led coalition exit.
A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight militants concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country’s leaders. Coalition troops were deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State group, which had seized large swathes of territory, committing massacres and forcing thousands of women and children into slavery. The group was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group’s remnants.
- The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Iran retaliates after Israeli strikes its nuclear program; 3 killed, several wounded.
Iran retaliated by launching drones and later firing waves of ballistic missiles at Israel, where explosions lit the night skies over Jerusalem and Tel Aviv and shook the buildings below
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Ahead of deal on Hormuz, US and Iran ramp up the rhetoric again.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Mystery over UK airbase scare as police find petrol not explosives.
A UK probe into a suspected bomb plot at an airbase used by the United States was mired in confusion, as police said no explosives but a “quantity of petrol” was found in vehicles seized nearby. Police were called to the Royal Air Force Fairford base in southwest England on Sunday after a resident saw several vans “acting suspiciously”, triggering an evacuation of the nearby village and the declaration of a “major incident”. “Those vehicles have been subject to extensive examination… and we can confirm that no improvised explosive devices were found.
India - bottom line: New NCERT book says Indian kings received swords from goddesses.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 21 hours ago: New NCERT book says Indian kings received swords from goddesses.
A new class nine social science textbook by NCERT titled 'Understanding Society: India and Beyond-Part 2' delves into India's historical experience with warfare. It emphasizes the cultural worship of deities like Kali and Durga for protection during conflicts, documents invasions from the seventh century, and highlights the valor of Indian rulers against foreign aggressors. This resource aims to enhance analytical thinking and foster intercultural dialogue among secondary students.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Russia's jet drones challenge Ukraine, India builds its own answer.
Russia's new Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones complicate Ukraine's air defense systems due to their high speed and altitude. Ukraine has started utilizing F-16 fighters and new interceptors to counter these advanced threats. Meanwhile, India's Defence Research and Development Organisation has developed a turbojet engine for future military applications. The Agniveg loitering munitions demonstrate India's capabilities to strike high-value targets efficiently.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Gary Sinise Foundation builds 100th mortgage-free smart home for wounded veteran.
After years of hesitance, Army veteran Joe Bowser has warmly welcomed a specially adapted smart home in Tennessee, crafted to support his mobility challenges. This poignant moment coincides with the 100th home delivered by the Gary Sinise Foundation for veterans. Bowser's family can now enjoy barrier-free space for togetherness. The deepening friendship between Bowser and Sinise, rooted in shared losses, emphasizes their mutual resilience and dedication to each other.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Ex-Pak SSG commando, LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind killed: Who was Moosa?.

- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: Ex-American Idol singer Caleb Flynn convicted of murdering wife, staging home invasion.
A former Ohio music pastor who once appeared on American Idol was convicted of murder on Tuesday in the killing of his wife while he was having an affair. Prosecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, staged a home invasion in February after shooting his wife, Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old teacher and volleyball coach. Taiwan’s military plans to spend more than NT$27 billion (US$850 million) to quadruple critical ammunition stocks to 120 days’ supply, strengthening its ability to sustain combat operations during a wartime blockade. The proposed six-year “urgent ammunition replenishment” programme, running from this year until 2031, comes as Taipei seeks to strengthen its ability to keep fighting if a cross-strait conflict cuts external supply lines. A computer simulation developed by Chinese researchers suggests that a missile-borne system with the latest light detection and ranging system, or lidar, could detect and track an F-35 stealth fighter at up to 61.5km (38 miles) at night. The theoretical model developed by a leading Chinese air force missile supplier says that under ideal conditions, the claimed range could have implications for the F-35’s ability to survive while facing China’s stealth fighters. While travelling in Kunming, southwestern China’s Yunnan province, a Chinese-Malaysian woman unexpectedly came across photos of her late grandfather showcased in a public exhibit. The display celebrated the historical contributions of overseas Chinese machinists who played a vital role in supporting the nation during World War II. Hannah Glover and James Sorgiovanni are accused of stabbing Busselton woman Tara Morrison multiple times before stuffing her body in a wardrobe.
